title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Indiana's 9th Congressional District
description: Indiana's 9th Congressional District stretches across south-central and southeastern Indiana, encompassing 18 counties including Monroe (Bloomington), Clark, Floyd, and Lawrence. Incumbent Republican Representative Erin Houchin, first elected in 2022 and serving as Secretary of the House Republican Conference, is running for a third term. She faces Democratic nominee Brad Meyer, a Purdue-trained engineer and former manufacturing leader who won a four-way primary on May 5, 2026, and Libertarian nominee Tonya Hudson, a real estate broker and perennial candidate. The district has leaned Republican in recent cycles — Houchin won with nearly 65% of the vote in 2024 — but Democrats see an opportunity to flip the seat in the midterm environment.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date.

candidates.name: Erin Houchin
candidates.summary: Erin Houchin is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Indiana's 9th District, first elected in 2022 after serving in the Indiana State Senate from 2014 to 2022. She serves on the House Committees on Education and Workforce, Financial Services, and Rules, and was elected Secretary of the House Republican Conference in November 2024. Her campaign emphasizes border security, cutting government spending, protecting the unborn, standing with Israel, and supporting conservative values and the Second Amendment.

candidates.name: Brad Meyer
candidates.summary: Brad Meyer is a seventh-generation Hoosier, Purdue-trained engineer, and the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 9th Congressional District. He spent 25 years in local manufacturing and six years as a civilian engineer at Crane Naval Sea Systems Command before retiring to run for Congress. His campaign focuses on universal nonprofit healthcare, expanding overtime protections, ending political gridlock, defending the Constitution, and protecting public education and the environment.

candidates.name: Tonya Hudson
candidates.summary: Tonya Hudson is a Libertarian candidate for Indiana's 9th Congressional District and a real estate broker of 21 years. She has run for Congress as a Libertarian in 2020 and 2022, and was Donald Rainwater's running mate for Lieutenant Governor in the 2024 Indiana gubernatorial election. Her campaign platform, branded 'Roll It Back,' calls for abolishing the IRS and replacing it with a FAIR/consumption tax, a balanced budget amendment, cutting regulatory red tape for small businesses, and protecting Second Amendment rights.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, so the forecast relies on structural and historical factors with limited confidence. Erin Houchin is the two-term incumbent, serves as Secretary of the House Republican Conference (a leadership post), and won the district with nearly 65% of the vote in 2024 — the strongest concrete signal in the record. The district (18 counties across south-central and southeastern Indiana, including Bloomington but otherwise largely rural and suburban) has leaned Republican in recent cycles. Democratic nominee Brad Meyer won a four-way primary in May 2026 and presents an articulate challenger, but there is no race-specific polling or fundraising data to suggest the race has become competitive. Libertarian Tonya Hudson is a perennial candidate who drew modest support in prior runs. The midterm environment may somewhat benefit Democrats nationally, but evidence to quantify a shift specific to IN-09 is absent. Accordingly, Republicans hold a clear but not overwhelming advantage, placing this race in the likely R band.
